subject: swordfish
title: A Swordfish Heats Its Own Eyes to See 10 Times Better in the Deep

scenes.text: This fish warms up its eyes before it hunts.
The swordfish dives several hundred metres down, into water as cold as 3 degrees Celsius. Down there, cold eyes see slowly: a darting squid becomes a blur.
So it cheats. A block of muscle beside each eye has been rewired into a heater. It burns energy and makes no movement, only warmth.
The heaters keep its eyes and brain up to 15 degrees warmer than the sea around it.
Warm retinas react faster. Researchers measured it: the swordfish sees fast-moving prey about ten times better than its cold-blooded prey can see it coming.
Everything else about it is cold. Only the eyes and brain run hot, exactly the parts that matter when you hunt in the dark.

description:
A swordfish has heater organs beside its eyes, made from modified eye muscle, that keep its eyes and brain up to 15 degrees Celsius warmer than the surrounding water.
It hunts several hundred metres down in water as cold as 3 degrees; the warm retinas react faster, and researchers at the University of Queensland measured a roughly tenfold improvement in its ability to see fast-moving prey such as squid (Fritsches et al., Current Biology, 2005).
Which other animal has a body part that runs on its own temperature?
first_comment: Marlin and some sharks have similar eye heaters, but the swordfish's is the biggest. Which deep-sea hunter should we cover next?
